target_customer: Biology and biotech labs that run experiments with robots and instruments
problem: Lab work is manual and fragmented across equipment, software and people, so biologists spend time programming robots and reconciling data instead of doing science.
business_model: B2B lab operating system software sold to labs (pricing not public)

founders.name: Dhasharath Shrivathsa
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder of Radix Labs (YC S18) with no career or education history.

founders.name: Ian Paul
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder with no bio.

competitors.name: Synthace
competitors.what: Antha, an operating system and programming language for biological experiments

competitors.name: Transcriptic
competitors.what: Robotic cloud lab service with TCLE and Autoprotocol software

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many vendors' lab instruments and robots behind one programmable layer needs device drivers, scheduling and reverse engineering, as its job postings (device drivers, reverse engineer, scheduling engineer) show.

defensibility.rationale: Deep instrument integrations could lock in labs, but each driver is replicable work and well funded rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying Radix.

market_need_then: Cloud lab and lab automation vendors such as Synthace and Transcriptic were drawing coverage in 2017, showing demand for software that programs lab robots.

branding.domain_note: Uses radix.bio rather than a .com; Radix is a common name shared with a blockchain company and others.

identity.logo: A 2020 identity by the studio Landscape, described as radically simple
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission line: make your labs work for you

rebrands.why: Design trade press covered a new visual identity by Landscape; the page itself could not be opened, so the reason is unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Only design trade coverage of the 2020 identity was found; the name is generic and confusable with other Radix companies.

outcome_analysis: Radix Labs raised a small seed in 2018 and about 2.87 million dollars in 2019 per one database, and rebranded in 2020, but the YC directory now lists it as inactive. No post-mortem, acquisition or layoff report was found, so the cause of the stall is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: radix.bio returned HTTP 503 so the site could not be read. Both rounds rest on a single database (CB Insights); investors are blank there. A Munich Startup profile shows a different split (120k grant, 2.9M seed, 4.0M Series A, 7.0M total) that no other source confirms; total raised is therefore uncertain and rounds may be missing. The Series A is unverified. The Synthace and Transcriptic article is dated April 2017 and does not mention Radix.
